chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, he said:

I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about madhy, and he instructed me to perform wudu (ablution) because of it. Then I repeated the question to him in another year, and he instructed me to perform wudu (ablution), and he said: Indeed, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام instructed al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad to ask the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and he was shy to ask him, so he said: Regarding it, there is wudu (ablution).

So this report does not conflict with what we have previously presented of the reports, because it is a solitary report. It also contains, in the account of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and his instructing al-Miqdād to ask the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and the Prophet’s reply to him, something that conflicts with what is well known in this account, namely that which is contained in the narration of Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār: that when he asked him, he said to him, “It is nothing.” It is also possible that the narrator omitted part of the report, because Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, the narrator of this report, narrated this very account itself, for he said: “He instructed me to repeat the wudu (ablution).” I said to him, “Then if I do not perform wudu (ablution)?” He said, “There is no harm.”

key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: title of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام in the report
key_terms.الْمَذْيِ: pre-seminal fluid discussed here as a matter of ritual purity
key_terms.الْمِقْدَادَ بْنَ الْأَسْوَدِ: the Companion sent to ask the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: ritual ablution mentioned as the act ordered in the report
key_terms.خَبَرٌ وَاحِدٌ: a solitary report, indicating a single-chain or non-mass-transmitted narration
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; indicating permissibility or absence of obligation

ai.seo_question: Does madhy require wudu (ablution) according to hadith in al-Istibṣār?
ai.summary: This report concerns the legal ruling on madhy and whether it necessitates wudu (ablution). The compiler explains that this narration is not taken as overriding other reports, noting both its solitary nature and another transmission indicating that leaving wudu in this case carries no harm.
